canonical.title: Maximum Path Sum in Binary Tree
canonical.sourceFilePath: 11. Binary Trees/2. Medium Problems/04. Maximum Path Sum.cpp

narrative.title: The Peak-Payout Delivery Route
narrative.scenario: A courier drone flies a binary-tree network of pickup towers, each carrying a parcel value that can be negative (a disposal fee). A route may start at any tower, follow connected links, and stop at any tower — but never revisits one. The dispatcher wants the maximum total value achievable, knowing sometimes the best route is a single tower and negative branches should be abandoned mid-flight.
narrative.inputFormat: The root of a binary tree given as a level-order array where null marks a missing child. Values may be negative.
narrative.outputFormat: Return an integer: the maximum sum of node values over any non-empty path in the tree.

testCases.explanation: The bend 2 -> 1 -> 3 collects all three positive towers.
Skip the negative root; the path 15 -> 20 -> 7 sums to 42.

hintLevels: Level 1: A path can bend at one node — it's a left descent plus the node plus a right descent, or any prefix of that.
Level 2: Clamp each child's contribution at 0: a negative branch is worth dropping entirely.
Level 3: Record node + max(0,left) + max(0,right) as the best bend here, but return only node + the better single branch — a path can't fork twice.
